title: CTS Pentateuch | Unit 12: Covenant Faithfulness — A Capstone

blocks.es_reference: Dr. Ted Rogers · Director del Seminario
Unidad 12 · Fidelidad al Pacto — Piedra Angular

blocks.en: 1. The Grand Narrative of the Pentateuch

You have traveled through Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy. You have seen the world created, humanity fallen, a covenant people called, enslaved, delivered, given the law, wandered in the wilderness, and finally poised at the border of the Promised Land. But the Pentateuch is not merely a collection of ancient stories. It is a unified drama with a single plot: God makes a covenant with His people, they break it, and God restores it — not because of their faithfulness, but because of His. From Genesis 3:15 (the seed of the woman who will crush the serpent's head) to the Passover lamb to the bronze serpent to the prophet like Moses, every page points to Jesus. The Pentateuch is the gospel in seed form. This final unit is not new content — it is a synthesis. We will trace the covenant from creation to the edge of Canaan, and we will see that the only faithful covenant keeper is God Himself — and ultimately, Jesus Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Has viajado a través de Génesis, Éxodo, Levítico, Números y Deuteronomio. Has visto el mundo creado, la humanidad caída, un pueblo del pacto llamado, esclavizado, liberado, recibiendo la ley, vagando por el desierto y finalmente detenido en la frontera de la Tierra Prometida. Pero el Pentateuco no es meramente una colección de historias antiguas. Es un drama unificado con una sola trama: Dios hace un pacto con Su pueblo, ellos lo rompen, y Dios lo restaura — no por la fidelidad de ellos, sino por la Suya. Desde Génesis 3:15 (la simiente de la mujer que aplastará la cabeza de la serpiente) hasta el cordero pascual, la serpiente de bronce y el profeta como Moisés, cada página apunta a Jesús. El Pentateuco es el evangelio en forma de semilla. Esta unidad final no es contenido nuevo — es una síntesis. Rastrearemos el pacto desde la creación hasta el borde de Canaán, y veremos que el único guardián fiel del pacto es Dios mismo — y finalmente, Jesucristo.

blocks.en: Genesis 3:15 (NKJV): "And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her Seed; He shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise His heel."
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 3:15 (RVG): "Y pondré enemistad entre ti y la mujer, y entre tu simiente y la simiente suya; ésta te herirá en la cabeza, y tú le herirás en el calcañar."

blocks.en: 2. Creation: Original Goodness and the Fall
blocks.es_reference: 2. Creación: La Bondad Original y la Caída

blocks.en: God created a perfect world, pronounced it "very good," and placed humanity as His image-bearers — living statues meant to remind creation of its Creator. But Adam and Eve rebelled. They ate the fruit. Shame, hiding, and blame followed. Yet even in judgment, God promised a deliverer. The seed of the woman would crush the serpent's head. The first gospel was preached not in a pulpit, but in a curse. This is the covenant framework: God initiates, God promises, and even when His people fail, God pursues. For the pastor, this is the foundation of every sermon: your people need to know that their salvation does not depend on their performance but on God's relentless covenant love.
blocks.es_reference: Dios creó un mundo perfecto, lo pronunció "muy bueno" y puso a la humanidad como sus portadores de imagen — estatuas vivientes destinadas a recordar a la creación a su Creador. Pero Adán y Eva se rebelaron. Comieron del fruto. La vergüenza, el escondite y la culpa siguieron. Pero incluso en el juicio, Dios prometió un libertador. La simiente de la mujer aplastaría la cabeza de la serpiente. El primer evangelio fue predicado no en un púlpito, sino en una maldición. Este es el marco del pacto: Dios inicia, Dios promete, e incluso cuando Su pueblo falla, Dios persigue. Para el pastor, este es el fundamento de cada sermón: tu gente necesita saber que su salvación no depende de su desempeño sino del amor del pacto implacable de Dios.

blocks.en: God called Abraham out of Ur, promising land, descendants, and blessing to all nations. Abraham believed, and God credited it to him as righteousness (Genesis 15:6) — the great proof-text for justification by faith. But Abraham failed. He lied about Sarah in Egypt. He took Hagar and fathered Ishmael. Yet God did not abandon him. He renewed the covenant, changed his name, and gave Isaac. The covenant was not conditioned on Abraham's obedience; it was unconditionally guaranteed by God's oath. The New Testament picks this up: we are children of Abraham not by blood but by faith (Galatians 3:7). Your congregation's security is not in their good works but in God's unbreakable promise.
blocks.es_reference: Dios llamó a Abraham fuera de Ur, prometiéndole tierra, descendientes y bendición a todas las naciones. Abraham creyó, y Dios se lo contó por justicia (Génesis 15:6) — el gran texto prueba de la justificación por la fe. Pero Abraham falló. Mintió sobre Sara en Egipto. Tomó a Agar y engendró a Ismael. Sin embargo, Dios no lo abandonó. Renovó el pacto, cambió su nombre y dio a Isaac. El pacto no estaba condicionado a la obediencia de Abraham; estaba garantizado incondicionalmente por el juramento de Dios. El Nuevo Testamento retoma esto: somos hijos de Abraham no por sangre sino por fe (Gálatas 3:7). La seguridad de tu congregación no está en sus buenas obras sino en la promesa inquebrantable de Dios.

blocks.en: Israel cried out in slavery. God heard and remembered His covenant. He sent Moses, performed signs and wonders, and delivered His people — not because they were worthy, but because He is faithful. The Passover lamb's blood marked the doorposts; judgment passed over. Paul says, "Christ, our Passover, was sacrificed for us" (1 Corinthians 5:7). The exodus is the great Old Testament picture of salvation: God saves by blood, not by human effort. Then He leads His people through the Red Sea (baptism), into the wilderness (testing), and toward the Promised Land (sanctification). The pastoral application is direct: your people did not earn their salvation. They were saved by the blood of the Lamb. Preach that again and again.
blocks.es_reference: Israel clamó en esclavitud. Dios escuchó y recordó Su pacto. Envió a Moisés, realizó señales y prodigios, y liberó a Su pueblo — no porque fueran dignos, sino porque Él es fiel. La sangre del cordero pascual marcó los postes de las puertas; el juicio pasó de largo. Pablo dice: "Cristo, nuestra pascua, fue sacrificado por nosotros" (1 Corintios 5:7). El éxodo es la gran imagen del Antiguo Testamento de la salvación: Dios salva por sangre, no por esfuerzo humano. Luego guía a Su pueblo a través del Mar Rojo (bautismo), al desierto (prueba) y hacia la Tierra Prometida (santificación). La aplicación pastoral es directa: tu gente no ganó su salvación. Fueron salvados por la sangre del Cordero. Predica eso una y otra vez.

blocks.en: 5. Sinai: The Law as Covenant Constitution
blocks.es_reference: 5. Sinaí: La Ley como Constitución del Pacto

blocks.en: At Mount Sinai, God gave the law — not as a means of salvation (they were already saved from Egypt), but as the constitution for their life as a nation. The Ten Commandments reveal God's character and show His people how to love Him and love neighbor. But the law also exposes sin. No one could keep it perfectly. The tabernacle, with its sacrifices and priesthood, provided a way for sinners to approach a holy God — by substitution. The bronze altar pointed to the cross; the mercy seat pointed to propitiation; the veil pointed to the barrier of sin that only Christ could tear down. For the pastor, the law drives your people to despair of self-righteousness and then the tabernacle points them to the substitute.
blocks.es_reference: En el Monte Sinaí, Dios dio la ley — no como medio de salvación (ya estaban salvados de Egipto), sino como la constitución para su vida como nación. Los Diez Mandamientos revelan el carácter de Dios y muestran a Su pueblo cómo amarlo a Él y amar al prójimo. Pero la ley también expone el pecado. Nadie podía guardarla perfectamente. El tabernáculo, con sus sacrificios y sacerdocio, proporcionaba un camino para que los pecadores se acercaran a un Dios santo — por sustitución. El altar de bronce apuntaba a la cruz; el propiciatorio apuntaba a la propiciación; el velo apuntaba a la barrera del pecado que solo Cristo podía rasgar. Para el pastor, la ley lleva a tu gente a la desesperación de la justicia propia y luego el tabernáculo los señala al sustituto.
6. Desierto: Incredulidad y Fidelidad de Dios

blocks.en: Numbers is the tragic record of a generation that saw miracles — manna, water from the rock, the pillar of cloud and fire — yet refused to trust God. Ten spies brought a bad report; the people believed them. God judged them with forty years of wandering until that generation died. But God did not abandon His covenant. He preserved Joshua and Caleb, and He raised up a new generation. The bronze serpent episode captures the gospel in miniature: the people sinned, God sent judgment (fiery serpents), then provided a cure (the serpent on a pole). All they had to do was look and live. Jesus said, "As Moses lifted up the serpent, so must the Son of Man be lifted up" (John 3:14). The pastoral lesson: unbelief disqualifies from blessing, but God always preserves a remnant of faith.
blocks.es_reference: Números es el registro trágico de una generación que vio milagros — maná, agua de la roca, la columna de nube y fuego — pero se negó a confiar en Dios. Diez espías trajeron mal informe; el pueblo les creyó. Dios los juzgó con cuarenta años de vagabundeo hasta que esa generación muriera. Pero Dios no abandonó Su pacto. Preservó a Josué y Caleb, y levantó una nueva generación. El episodio de la serpiente de bronce captura el evangelio en miniatura: el pueblo pecó, Dios envió juicio (serpientes ardientes), luego proveyó una cura (la serpiente en un asta). Todo lo que tenían que hacer era mirar y vivir. Jesús dijo: "Como Moisés levantó la serpiente en el desierto, así es necesario que el Hijo del Hombre sea levantado" (Juan 3:14). La lección pastoral: la incredulidad descalifica de la bendición, pero Dios siempre preserva un remanente de fe.

blocks.en: Pastoral Reflection: The wilderness generation had every advantage — they saw the Red Sea part, ate manna, drank from the rock. Yet they perished because of unbelief. Your congregation has advantages too: Bibles, sermons, testimonies. Do not let them assume that knowledge equals faith. Warn them. Love them. Point them to Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Reflexión Pastoral: La generación del desierto tenía todas las ventajas — vieron el Mar Rojo abrirse, comieron maná, bebieron de la roca. Pero perecieron por incredulidad. Tu congregación también tiene ventajas: Biblias, sermones, testimonios. No dejes que asuman que el conocimiento es igual a la fe. Advierte. Ama. Señala a Cristo.

blocks.en: 7. Deuteronomy: Covenant Renewal and the Choice of Life
blocks.es_reference: 7. Deuteronomio: Renovación del Pacto y la Elección de la Vida

blocks.en: On the plains of Moab, Moses preached his final sermons. He reviewed the law, called the new generation to covenant faithfulness, and set before them a choice: "I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing; therefore choose life" (Deuteronomy 30:19). But how could they choose life? They were sinners. The law cursed all who did not keep it perfectly. The answer is that the law was never meant to be kept in human strength. The law drives us to the gospel. Moses promised a prophet like himself — fulfilled in Jesus (Acts 3:22-23). And Moses himself, the great lawgiver, died outside the land. Only Joshua (Yeshua — "The Lord saves") could lead them in. The name Joshua is the Hebrew equivalent of Jesus. The Pentateuch ends with hope: a new leader, a new generation, and the promise that God will be with them.
blocks.es_reference: En las llanuras de Moab, Moisés predicó sus sermones finales. Repasó la ley, llamó a la nueva generación a la fidelidad del pacto, y puso delante de ellos una elección: "He puesto delante de ti la vida y la muerte, la bendición y la maldición; escoge, pues, la vida" (Deuteronomio 30:19). Pero ¿cómo podían elegir la vida? Eran pecadores. La ley maldecía a todos los que no la guardaban perfectamente. La respuesta es que la ley nunca tuvo la intención de ser guardada con fuerza humana. La ley nos lleva al evangelio. Moisés prometió un profeta como él — cumplido en Jesús (Hechos 3:22-23). Y el mismo Moisés, el gran legislador, murió fuera de la tierra. Solo Josué (Yeshua — "El Señor salva") podía guiarlos. El nombre Josué es el equivalente hebreo de Jesús. El Pentateuco termina con esperanza: un nuevo líder, una nueva generación y la promesa de que Dios estará con ellos.

blocks.en: Deuteronomy 30:19-20 (NKJV): "I call heaven and earth as witnesses today against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing; therefore choose life, that both you and your descendants may live; that you may love the Lord your God, that you may obey His voice, and that you may cling to Him, for He is your life."
blocks.es_reference: Deuteronomio 30:19-20 (RVG): "A los cielos y a la tierra llamo por testigos hoy contra vosotros, que os he puesto delante la vida y la muerte, la bendición y la maldición; escoge, pues, la vida, para que vivas tú y tu descendencia; amando a Jehová tu Dios, atendiendo a su voz, y siguiéndole a él; porque él es tu vida."

blocks.en: 8. Typology: The Pentateuch Is About Jesus
blocks.es_reference: 8. Tipología: El Pentateuco Trata de Jesús

blocks.en: Jesus Himself said, "If you believed Moses, you would believe Me, for he wrote about Me" (John 5:46). The Pentateuch is Christ-centered. Adam is a type of Christ (Romans 5). Melchizedek prefigures Jesus' eternal priesthood (Hebrews 7). Isaac carried wood up Moriah, pointing to the beloved Son carrying His cross. The Passover lamb is explicitly identified with Christ (1 Corinthians 5:7). The rock that gave water was Christ (1 Corinthians 10:4). The bronze serpent lifted up prefigures the crucifixion (John 3:14-15). The prophet like Moses is Jesus (Acts 3:22-23). The tabernacle and its sacrifices are shadows of heavenly realities (Hebrews 8-10). And Joshua (Yeshua) leads the people into the Promised Land — just as Jesus leads His people into eternal rest. To miss Christ in the Pentateuch is to miss the point entirely. Pastors, do not preach the Old Testament as moralistic tales. Preach it as a gallery of portraits of your Savior.
blocks.es_reference: Jesús mismo dijo: "Si creyerais a Moisés, me creeríais a mí, porque de mí escribió él" (Juan 5:46). El Pentateuco está centrado en Cristo. Adán es un tipo de Cristo (Romanos 5). Melquisedec prefigura el sacerdocio eterno de Jesús (Hebreos 7). Isaac cargó la leña por Moriah, apuntando al Hijo amado que carga su cruz. El cordero pascual es explícitamente identificado con Cristo (1 Corintios 5:7). La roca que dio agua era Cristo (1 Corintios 10:4). La serpiente de bronce levantada prefigura la crucifixión (Juan 3:14-15). El profeta como Moisés es Jesús (Hechos 3:22-23). El tabernáculo y sus sacrificios son sombras de realidades celestiales (Hebreos 8-10). Y Josué (Yeshua) guía al pueblo a la Tierra Prometida — así como Jesús guía a Su pueblo al reposo eterno. Perder a Cristo en el Pentateuco es perder el punto por completo. Pastores, no prediquen el Antiguo Testamento como cuentos moralistas. Predíquenlo como una galería de retratos de su Salvador.

blocks.en: 9. Application: What the Pentateuch Produces in God's People
blocks.es_reference: 9. Aplicación: Lo Que el Pentateuco Produce en el Pueblo de Dios

blocks.en: A steady diet of the Pentateuch produces five things in your congregation. First, wonder — they see the majesty of God who created the cosmos and called a people for Himself. Second, humility — they see their own sin in the golden calf, in the grumbling, in the rebellion of Korah, and they cry out for mercy. Third, gratitude — they see that God delivered Israel not because they were worthy, and He saved them not because they were righteous, but because He is gracious. Fourth, hope — they see that even when God's people fail, God does not abandon His covenant. He disciplines, He restores, He raises up new leaders. Fifth, faith — they see that the entire Old Testament sacrificial system pointed to Jesus, and they rest in His finished work. Preach the Pentateuch, and you will not produce legalists. You will produce people who love God, trust His promises, and cling to Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Una dieta constante del Pentateuco produce cinco cosas en tu congregación. Primero, asombro — ven la majestad de Dios que creó el cosmos y llamó a un pueblo para Sí mismo. Segundo, humildad — ven su propio pecado en el becerro de oro, en la murmuración, en la rebelión de Coré, y claman por misericordia. Tercero, gratitud — ven que Dios liberó a Israel no porque eran dignos, y los salvó no porque eran justos, sino porque Él es misericordioso. Cuarto, esperanza — ven que incluso cuando el pueblo de Dios falla, Dios no abandona Su pacto. Disciplina, restaura, levanta nuevos líderes. Quinto, fe — ven que todo el sistema sacrificial del Antiguo Testamento apuntaba a Jesús, y descansan en Su obra terminada. Predica el Pentateuco, y no producirás legalistas. Producirás personas que aman a Dios, confían en Sus promesas y se aferran a Cristo.

blocks.en: Final Charge: You have completed this course. But the Pentateuch is not a box to check. It is the foundation of your ministry. Let these five books shape your preaching, your counseling, your leadership, and your own soul. Moses saw the Promised Land from Mount Nebo but did not enter. You will not see the full fruit of your ministry in this life. But you will see it from afar — and one day, you will enter the true Promised Land, where the Lamb who was slain is the light of the city. Until then, preach Christ from all the Scriptures. Start with Moses.
blocks.es_reference: Encargo Final: Has completado este curso. Pero el Pentateuco no es una casilla que marcar. Es el fundamento de tu ministerio. Deja que estos cinco libros moldeen tu predicación, tu consejería, tu liderazgo y tu propia alma. Moisés vio la Tierra Prometida desde el Monte Nebo pero no entró. No verás todo el fruto de tu ministerio en esta vida. Pero lo verás de lejos — y un día, entrarás en la verdadera Tierra Prometida, donde el Cordero que fue inmolado es la luz de la ciudad. Hasta entonces, predica a Cristo desde todas las Escrituras. Empieza con Moisés.

blocks.en: Before he died, Moses blessed the tribes of Israel (Deuteronomy 33). I leave you with a blessing drawn from the words of the Pentateuch: "The Lord bless you and keep you; the Lord make His face shine upon you, and be gracious to you; the Lord lift up His countenance upon you, and give you peace" (Numbers 6:24-26). May you know that you are made as the image of God (Genesis 1:26). May you trust the blood of the Passover Lamb (Exodus 12). May you drink water from the Rock who is Christ (1 Corinthians 10:4). May you look to the bronze serpent and live (Numbers 21:8-9). May you love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and strength (Deuteronomy 6:5). And may you rest in the finished work of Jesus, the Seed of the woman, the Prophet like Moses, our great High Priest, the Lamb of God. Amen.
blocks.es_reference: Antes de morir, Moisés bendijo a las tribus de Israel (Deuteronomio 33). Te dejo con una bendición extraída de las palabras del Pentateuco: "Jehová te bendiga, y te guarde; Jehová haga resplandecer su rostro sobre ti, y tenga de ti misericordia; Jehová alce sobre ti su rostro, y ponga en ti paz" (Números 6:24-26). Que sepas que eres hecho como imagen de Dios (Génesis 1:26). Que confíes en la sangre del Cordero Pascual (Éxodo 12). Que bebas agua de la Roca que es Cristo (1 Corintios 10:4). Que mires a la serpiente de bronce y vivas (Números 21:8-9). Que ames a Jehová tu Dios con todo tu corazón, alma y fuerzas (Deuteronomio 6:5). Y que descanses en la obra terminada de Jesús, la Simiente de la mujer, el Profeta como Moisés, nuestro gran Sumo Sacerdote, el Cordero de Dios. Amén.

mc.stem: What is the unifying plot of the Pentateuch?
options: God makes a covenant, people break it, God restores it by His faithfulness
mc.why: Correct! The Pentateuch is the story of God's covenant faithfulness despite human failure.

mc.stem: Where is the first gospel promise found in the Pentateuch?
mc.why: Yes. The seed of the woman will crush the serpent's head — the first announcement of a Savior.

mc.stem: What event does Paul explicitly identify as a type of Christ in 1 Corinthians 5:7?
mc.why: Correct. 'Christ, our Passover, was sacrificed for us.'

mc.stem: How did Abraham receive righteousness according to Genesis 15:6?
mc.why: Yes. 'He believed in the Lord, and He accounted it to him for righteousness.'

mc.stem: What did the blood on the doorposts at the first Passover signify?
options: The angel of death would pass over that house
mc.why: Yes. 'When I see the blood, I will pass over you.' Salvation by substitution.

mc.stem: According to 1 Corinthians 10:4, what was the rock that followed Israel?
mc.why: Correct. 'That Rock was Christ.'

mc.stem: What did people have to do to be healed from the fiery serpents (Numbers 21)?
options: Look at the bronze serpent on a pole
mc.why: Yes. Look and live — a picture of faith.

mc.stem: How did Jesus apply the bronze serpent to Himself in John 3?
options: 'As Moses lifted up the serpent, so must the Son of Man be lifted up'
mc.why: Yes. The crucifixion is the ultimate 'lifting up' for healing.

mc.stem: What does the name 'Joshua' (Hebrew: Yeshua) mean?
mc.why: Yes. Yeshua is the Hebrew form of Jesus. Joshua leads Israel into the land; Jesus leads us into eternal rest.

mc.stem: What prophet did Moses promise in Deuteronomy 18?
mc.why: Yes. 'A Prophet like you' — fulfilled in Jesus (Acts 3:22-23).

mc.stem: Who was Melchizedek, and why is he significant?
options: King of Salem and priest of God Most High — a type of Christ's eternal priesthood
mc.why: Yes. Hebrews 7 explains that Jesus is a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.

mc.stem: What did Isaac carry up Mount Moriah?
options: The wood for his own sacrifice
mc.why: Yes. Isaac carried the wood — a type of Christ carrying His cross.

mc.stem: What happened to the veil of the temple when Jesus died?
options: It was torn in two from top to bottom
mc.why: Yes. The torn veil symbolizes direct access to God through Christ's sacrifice.

mc.stem: According to Deuteronomy 30:19, what choice did God set before Israel?
options: Life and death, blessing and cursing — choose life
mc.why: Yes. But they could not choose life in their own strength — they needed a Savior.

mc.stem: How does the Pentateuch produce humility in God's people?
options: By showing their ancestors were perfect
By commanding them to be humble
By showing repeated failures — golden calf, grumbling, unbelief
mc.why: Yes. Seeing Israel's rebellion shows us our own sin and need for grace.

mc.stem: What does the mercy seat (the cover of the Ark) foreshadow?
options: Propitiation — Christ is the place where God's justice and mercy meet
mc.why: Yes. Christ is our propitiation (Romans 3:25).

mc.stem: According to the lesson, what should pastors preach from the Old Testament?
options: Only the laws that apply today
Christ — He is the point of every passage
Only the narrative, not the law
mc.why: Yes. Jesus said Moses wrote about Him. Preach Christ from the Pentateuch.

mc.stem: What is the meaning of the name 'Yeshua' (Joshua/Jesus)?
mc.why: Yes. Jesus' name means 'The Lord saves' — exactly what He came to do.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, what is one result of preaching the Pentateuch faithfully?
options: Faith in Christ, hope in God's promises, and love for God
mc.why: Yes. The Pentateuch, properly preached, leads people to Christ, not to legalism.

mc.stem: What blessing ends the lesson and the course?
mc.why: Yes. 'The Lord bless you and keep you...'

sa.prompt: Summarize the grand narrative of the Pentateuch in one paragraph.
sa.model: God creates, humanity falls, God calls Abraham, redeems Israel from Egypt, gives the law, disciplines in the wilderness, and brings them to the border of Canaan — all pointing to Christ.

sa.prompt: Explain Genesis 3:15 as the protoevangelium (first gospel).
sa.model: God promises that the offspring of the woman will crush the serpent's head — the first announcement of a coming Savior, fulfilled in Christ.

sa.prompt: How does the Passover lamb point to Jesus (1 Corinthians 5:7)?
sa.model: The unblemished lamb dies in place of the firstborn; its blood protects from judgment. Paul explicitly calls Christ 'our Passover.'

sa.prompt: What does the bronze serpent teach about salvation (John 3:14-15)?
sa.model: The serpent represented the curse; lifted up, it became the cure. Jesus became a curse for us; whoever looks to Him in faith lives — no works required.

sa.prompt: How is Melchizedek a type of Christ (Hebrews 7)?
sa.model: Melchizedek was both king and priest, had no recorded beginning or end, received tithes from Abraham, and brought bread and wine — all prefiguring Christ's eternal priesthood.

sa.prompt: Why did Moses not enter the Promised Land, and what does this teach about leadership?
sa.model: Moses struck the rock in anger instead of speaking to it, dishonoring God's holiness. Leaders face consequences, but God's work continues through successors.

sa.prompt: What is the significance of the name 'Joshua' (Yeshua) and how does it connect to Jesus?
sa.model: Yeshua means 'The Lord saves.' Joshua led Israel into the earthly Promised Land; Jesus (the same name) leads His people into eternal salvation and rest.

sa.prompt: What choice did God set before Israel in Deuteronomy 30:19, and why could they not choose life on their own?
sa.model: God set life and death before them, but fallen humanity cannot keep the law perfectly. The command drives them to seek the Savior who keeps it for them.

sa.prompt: List the five things the Pentateuch produces in God's people when preached Christologically.
sa.model: Wonder at God's majesty, humility from seeing sin, gratitude for undeserved grace, hope that God keeps covenant, and faith in Christ as the fulfillment.

sa.prompt: Why did Jesus say, 'If you believed Moses, you would believe Me, for he wrote about Me' (John 5:46)?
sa.model: The entire Pentateuch — its laws, sacrifices, and narratives — was designed to point to Jesus. To read Moses and miss Christ is to misread Moses entirely.
